body.text: Passengers decribe chaos on commercial flight as pilot stabs colleague and tries to crash plane
In short:
Benjamin Netanyahu says a pilot on a commercial flight carrying 174 people has stabbed the other pilot and tried to crash the jet.
Passengers on the flight had to hold the alleged attacker down, according to the Israeli PM.
The airline, flydubai, says a "formal investigation" is underway, while Israeli officials are treating it as a terror attack.

A commercial flight carrying 174 people and bound for Tel Aviv had to divert to Saudi Arabia after one pilot stabbed the other and "apparently tried to crash the plane", according to Israel's prime minister.
Warning: This article contains graphic images.
The Boeing 737, operated by flydubai, a sister airline of Emirates, took off from Dubai International Airport in the United Arab Emirates on Wednesday morning, local time.
Tabuk Airport, in north-west Saudi Arabia, said its air-traffic control received a distress call from the flight FZ1073 at 8:44am, local time. It landed there safely about an hour later.
The majority of the passengers were Israeli. The nation's authorities are treating the emergency as a terror attack.

In a video address released by his office on Wednesday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu made several startling claims about what he described as a "highly severe security incident". He said:
• One pilot stabbed the other and attempted to crash the plane.
• The flight entered a "tailspin", which prompted passengers to break into the cockpit with a member of the crew.
• Once inside, the group found a co-pilot "trying to sabotage the plane's systems".
• The plane only landed safely because other people took control.
Almost all the passengers on the flight were Israeli, Mr Netanyahu said, before praising the group that intervened at the front of the plane.
"They saved many lives," he said. "They prevented a heavy disaster."
He also said Saudi officials had arrested one of the pilots.
Citing local security sources, Israeli media outlets and Reuters said the incident was being treated as a terror attack.
Authorities would "ramp up" flight security on Israeli and non-Israeli carriers, Mr Netanyahu's spokesman later added.
According to the website Flightradar24, the flydubai plane plunged about 4,000 metres in less than 30 seconds at one point during its journey.
Some of the details from Mr Netanyahu's video were corroborated by a flydubai spokesperson, who said an "altercation had occurred" on the flightdeck of FZ1073.
"At this early stage, the underlying reasons and motives behind this event are unknown and remain subject to a formal investigation," they said.
Passengers on the diverted flight later arrived at Tel Aviv's Ben Gurion Airport, where they were greeted by friends and family.
One of the passengers was later pictured with Mr Netanyahu. The prime minister's office released images of the meeting on X, saying the passenger helped burst into the cockpit during the incident.
Mr Netanyahu has warned people could try to attack his country ahead of its elections, due to be held next month.
'We jumped and helped the pilot'
Verified images from inside the flight showed men covered in blood.

One of the passengers on board, Itzhak Liber, posted a video to social media shortly before the plane landed, in which he said: "We are here on the plane. There was a crazy man with a knife who stabbed one of the pilots.

"We jumped and helped the pilot. Friends, everything is OK now. As you can see, we are landing in Saudi Arabia. You can see I am fine. That's it. We will see in a few minutes what will happen when we land."
Another man on the flight said in a video posted online: "We control the flight, we controlled the terrorists. Anyone who can hear me, we need help."
A third passenger posted on social media that he saw a "riot" at the front of the plane and that a third pilot onboard "managed to take control of the aircraft and take us south to Saudi Arabia".

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz on Wednesday described the incident as "a jihadist terror attempt" which was "thwarted only thanks to the bravery of several Israeli passengers who broke into the cockpit".
Transporting the passengers from Tabuk to Tel Aviv has been complicated by Saudi Arabia and Israel not having formal diplomatic relations.
An Israeli request to send a plane to pick up the passengers was rejected. Flydubai said it sent two planes to Tabuk later on Wednesday to pick up the stranded people.
Former commercial pilot Terry Tozer said it was pure chance that the incident did not end in a major tragedy, praising the actions of the crew who took control and safely landed the aircraft.
"Falling at that altitude would have been terrifying," he said.
"You can just imagine, if the aircraft pitches down and keeps going, it's going to be pretty scary."

Mr Tozer, who wrote the book Confessions of an Airline Pilot: Why Planes Crash, said the structural damage caused by the rapid 4,000-metre descent would have made stabilising the aircraft dramatically more challenging.

"The aircraft has been subjected to colossal forces," he told the ABC. "You can't make anything completely unbreakable, and as we saw from photos, it appears as if the plane lost its rudder at some point during this process.
"It is possible to suffer an in-flight break-up, with the aircraft coming apart if design limits are exceeded."
He said the person who changed the pitch of the plane by pulling back on the altitude controls had kept their cool.
"Whoever pulled it back didn't do it too aggressively because something else might have gone wrong," Mr Tozer said.
